Google Cloud: Artifact Registry ​

Verified against primary documentation on 2026-10-16.

Names ​

An image is addressed as LOCATION-docker.pkg.dev/PROJECT-ID/REPOSITORY/IMAGE, with :TAG or @IMAGE-DIGEST after it. The location is the first part of the hostname, "the regional or multi-regional location of the repository" (Repository and image names). IMAGE is "the name of the image in the repository". The project and the repository are therefore both fixed before our own path starts, which is why the ADR treats <location>-docker.pkg.dev/<project> as the registry prefix.

Not stated by Google, so not verified:

  • The character grammar of a repository name. The create guide says only that "For each repository location in a project, repository names must be unique" (Create standard repositories), and the REST reference describes repositoryId as "The repository id to use for this repository" with no constraint (repositories.create). The lowercase [a-z0-9-] rule in the ADR is our own and sits inside any plausible grammar, but Google's grammar is not documented in the pages checked.
  • Length limits for repository, image or tag names. No page checked states one, and the quotas page was not reachable.
  • Whether a standard repository accepts an image name with / in it. The only nested example is a remote repository that proxies GitHub Container Registry, pulled as us-west1-docker.pkg.dev/my-project/my-repo/owner-name/test-image:staging (Push and pull images). The ADR's paths images/<namespace>/<name>, charts/<namespace>/<name> and wasm-components/<namespace>/<package> rely on a nested image name in a standard repository, so this stays unverified.

Repositories ​

Each repository holds one format: "Each repository can contain artifacts for a single supported format", and the formats include Docker, Generic, Maven, npm and Python (Create standard repositories). The Docker quickstart creates the repository first ("Create a Docker repository to store the sample image"), and the push guide says "If the target repository does not exist, create a new repository" (Push and pull images). The one exception is the legacy gcr.io domain, whose repositories are created on first push (Repository overview). No page checked says outright that a push to a missing repository on docker.pkg.dev fails, so "must be created first" rests on the guides above.

Helm charts and other OCI artifacts live in Docker-format repositories. The supported formats page says "Store Docker container images and Helm charts packaged in OCI format" and "You can store artifacts that support the OCI image format in Artifact Registry Docker repositories" (Supported formats). The Helm guide repeats it: "Artifact Registry lets you store and manage Helm charts in Docker-format repositories", pushed with helm push hello-chart-0.1.0.tgz oci://us-west1-docker.pkg.dev/PROJECT/quickstart-helm-repo. "The chart name is the image name" and "The chart version is the image tag" (Store Helm charts), which matches the ADR's description of what Helm appends.

Not verified: Wasm components. No page checked mentions Wasm. They are OCI artifacts, so the general OCI statement above is the only support, and no Google page promises that a wkg push of a Wasm media type is accepted.

One repository per kind (images, charts, wasm-components) is therefore allowed but not required: a single Docker-format repository could hold all of them. Separate repositories are our choice, and they are what let cleanup policies and IAM differ per kind.

Remote repositories ​

Remote repositories "act as proxies" and are read-only. On the first request the repository "downloads and caches" the artifact, and "Artifact Registry serves the cached copy" for the same version afterwards (Repository overview, Remote repositories overview).

  • One upstream per repository. No page states the count in words. The upstream is a single setting ("Remote repository upstream source") that "can't be changed after the repository is created", the gcloud flag --remote-docker-repo takes one value, docker-hub or one HTTPS URI, and the preset for Docker Hub is DOCKER-HUB at https://registry-1.docker.io (Create remote repositories, gcloud create). A virtual repository is the product that aggregates several upstreams. So mirrors-docker-hub and mirrors-quay as separate remote repositories follows from the design, but it is an inference.
  • Tag refresh. Mutable metadata "are updated from the upstream source when they become more than the default age", and the listed default for the Docker tag list cache is 1 hour (Remote repositories overview). The quickstart says "If you pull the same tagged image again, it will be pulled from your remote repository" (Docker Hub remote quickstart). No page says when an already cached tag is moved to a new upstream digest, so the ADR's statement that a cache refresh moves a mirrored tag is not confirmed, and the 1 hour figure covers the tag list only.
  • Path. The quickstart pulls us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/PROJECT/quickstart-docker-hub-remote/busybox:latest, with no library/ segment. No page checked mentions library/. This does not confirm the ADR's mirrors-docker-hub/library/postgres:16, and it suggests the bare mirrors-docker-hub/postgres:16 may be what Artifact Registry expects for Docker Hub official images. It needs a live pull to settle.

Tag immutability ​

The setting is Immutable image tags, for Docker repositories only, and it is off by default. When on, these actions are not permitted: "Delete a tagged image", "Remove a tag from an image", "Push an image with a tag that is already used by another version of the image in the repository", and "Add, remove, or update labels". The page adds that a tag always points to the same digest, "including the default latest tag" (Configure repository settings, Create standard repositories). In gcloud it is --immutable-tags ("Tags cannot be deleted or moved to a different image digest, and tagged images cannot be deleted") and --no-immutable-tags (gcloud create).

No page checked describes any exemption, allowlist or pattern for tags, which supports the ADR's claim that none can be exempted. This is absence of documentation, not a stated "cannot".

The setting is also a Docker-repository setting, so it is not documented as applying to a remote repository. The ADR already exempts mirrors from the tag rules.

Consequence for cleanup: "If a repository has immutable tags enabled, tagged artifacts can't be deleted" (Cleanup policies). With immutability on, a cleanup policy cannot expire pr- tags. See the next section.

Cleanup policies ​

A policy is a Delete or a Keep action plus conditions (Configure cleanup policies):

ConditionMeaning
tagStatetagged, untagged or any
tagPrefixestag prefixes, needs tagState set to tagged
versionNamePrefixesversion name prefixes
packageNamePrefixespackage name prefixes
olderThanminimum time since the version was created, as a duration
newerThanmaximum time since the version was created
keepCountkeep the most recent versions, a keep policy only

Prefixes match the start of a tag: "the prefixes test, and staging would match images with tags testenv and staging-1.5". "If an artifact matches the criteria in both the delete policy and the keep policy, the artifact is kept", and a keep policy alone has no effect, so at least one delete policy must exist. The page's example deletes "tagPrefixes": ["alpha", "v0"] with "olderThan": "30d" and keeps release-prefixed tags. Changes take effect "within approximately one day", and a dry run is available.

So expiring pr- and 0.0.0-pr- builds is a delete policy with tagState: tagged, the two prefixes and an olderThan. Release tags are never matched by those prefixes, and a keep policy on the version tags is available as a second guard. This composition is an inference from the documented conditions. The page has no pr- example.

Open points:

  • The page says "You can only apply cleanup policies to standard repositories", yet the remote repository guide lists cleanup policies as an optional setting at creation. The two are not reconciled by the pages checked, so cleanup on mirrors-* repositories is unverified.
  • The commit-tagged image of a pull request carries only pr-<commit>, but an image that later gets a release tag is a different tag on the same version. Whether a version is deleted when any one of its tags matches a delete policy and none matches a keep policy is not spelled out.
  • Cleanup does not apply to attachments directly (see the next section).
  • Because immutable tags block deletion of tagged artifacts, a repository cannot both turn on immutability and expire pr- tags by cleanup policy. This follows from the quoted sentence, but no page shows the two together.

Signatures and referrers ​

Artifact Registry "implements version 1.1 of the Open Container Initiative (OCI) Distribution Specification" (Support for the Docker Registry API). That page does not name the referrers endpoint.

Attachments are the documented mechanism: "Artifact Registry attachments let you store and manage metadata files associated with your artifacts", and an artifact can have "any number of attachments that refer to it". They can be listed with Oras and the v1.1-referrers-api distribution spec, for Docker container images, and the page is marked pre-GA. "Cleanup policies don't apply directly to attachments", and deleting an artifact deletes the attachments that target its version (Manage artifact metadata).

Binary Authorization's Sigstore check keeps cosign signatures alongside the image in the same Artifact Registry repository, and supports only Artifact Registry repositories (Use the Sigstore signature check). Cosign lists Artifact Registry among the registries it was tested against (Cosign registry support).

Not verified:

  • That the /v2/<name>/referrers/<digest> endpoint itself is served. The attachments page uses it through Oras, which implies it, but no Google page states it.
  • Whether signatures and referrers survive inside a remote repository, or are copied with an image into another registry. The ADR's rule to copy them with the artifact is a client concern and is not covered by Google pages.
